title: Timeout-bounded job runner
prompt:
Implement `async def with_timeout(job, seconds)`:

- run the zero-arg async callable `job` under `asyncio.timeout(seconds)`
- return the job's value when it finishes in time
- return exactly the string `f'timeout:{seconds}'` when it exceeds the budget

tests.name: fast job passes through
tests.code:
async def quick():
    await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
    return 7

loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
assert loop.run_until_complete(with_timeout(quick, 1)) == 7
loop.close()
print('ok')
tests.hint: The timeout context wraps the await of the job itself.

tests.name: slow job returns the sentinel
tests.code:
async def slow():
    await asyncio.sleep(5)
    return 'late'

loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
assert loop.run_until_complete(with_timeout(slow, 0.05)) == 'timeout:0.05', 'must return the sentinel'
loop.close()
print('ok')
tests.hint: asyncio.timeout cancels the inner task at the deadline and raises TimeoutError inside the with.
